chunks: And from him, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Allan, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yazid, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "If one of you were to perform Hajj for his entire life, and then did not visit al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), he would be leaving a right from the rights of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), because the right of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) is a divine obligation obligatory upon every Muslim."

key_terms.حُقُوق: Rights (plural of haqq, referring to due obligations)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (specifically to the shrines of Imams)

ai.seo_question: Is visiting Imam Husayn's shrine obligatory for Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates Ziyarat al-Husayn from a recommended act to a mandatory obligation (fariḍah), linking it directly to the rights of the Prophet. This establishes that neglecting the visit of Imam al-Husayn constitutes a deficiency in fulfilling one's duty to the Messenger of Allah, regardless of the volume of other worship like Hajj. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Ahl al-Bayt are the continuing manifestation of the Prophet's legacy and authority.
